title: A practical website review for a busy business owner
summary: Review your website through a customer’s eyes, from the first impression to the final enquiry.
author: ARA Editorial
answer: Start on your phone and follow a realistic customer journey. Check that your services are clear, essential information is easy to find, links work and the enquiry process gives an honest result.

sections.heading: Can someone understand your offer?
paragraphs: Open the homepage and read the first heading and paragraph. Do they explain the business and its services? A visually impressive page still needs to answer the visitor’s basic questions.
Check whether your service area and contact route are easy to find. Use confirmed business details rather than filling gaps with generic claims.

sections.heading: Can they find the detail?
paragraphs: Choose one service and follow the navigation. Look for a description, scope, relevant examples and the next step. Check that important information is text that can be read and selected, rather than only text inside an image.
Then repeat the journey on a smaller screen. A menu that works with a mouse can still be difficult to use by touch or keyboard.

sections.heading: Does the enquiry journey work?
paragraphs: Submit a test enquiry using a test mailbox you control. Confirm that it was saved, that the team can retrieve it and that any promised confirmation arrives. A success message on its own does not prove delivery.
Only ask for the information you need at this stage. Explain how enquiry details are used and make the privacy information available before submission.

sections.heading: Turn findings into a manageable plan
paragraphs: Group your findings by impact. Broken enquiry forms and inaccessible service information usually deserve attention before decorative refinements. Assign an owner and a clear completion check to each change.

Revisit the journey after updates. Keep a simple record of what changed, what was verified and what still needs work. A website review is most valuable when it leads to a manageable sequence of improvements.
